Faithful hearts are comparatively common--but when a man is faithful with his brain....”

arxiv-1803-01783.title: Dynamic Competition Networks: detecting alliances and leaders Thanks: Research supported by grants from NSERC, Ryerson University, NSF CCF-1149756, IIS-1546488, NSF Center for Science of Information, CCF-0939370, DARPA SIMPLEX.
arxiv-1803-01783.creator: Anthony Bonato, Nicole Eikmeier, David F. Gleich, Rehan Malik
arxiv-1803-01783.description: Abstract We consider social networks of competing agents that evolve dynamically over time. Such dynamic competition networks are directed, where a directed edge from nodes u u to v v corresponds a negative social interaction. We present a novel hypothesis that serves as a predictive tool to uncover alliances and leaders within dynamic competition networks.

arxiv-2106-14410.description: Abstract Motivated by the growing evidence for the possible lepton flavour universality violation after the first results from Fermilab’s muon ( g − 2 ) (g-2) measurement, we revisit one of the most widely studied anomaly free extensions of the standard model namely, gauged L μ − L τ L_{\mu}-L_{\tau} model, to find a common explanation for muon ( g

arxiv-2108-06381.title: Political Districting without Geography
arxiv-2108-06381.creator: Gerdus Benadè, Nam Ho-Nguyen, J. N. Hooker
arxiv-2108-06381.description: Abstract Geographical considerations such as contiguity and compactness are necessary elements of political districting in practice. Yet an analysis of the problem without such constraints yields mathematical insights that can inform real-world model construction. In particular, it clarifies the sharp contrast between proportionality and competitiveness and how it might be overcome in a properly formulated objective function.

arxiv-2209-12269.title: Algorithms that Approximate Data Removal: New Results and Limitations
arxiv-2209-12269.creator: Vinith M. Suriyakumar, Ashia C. Wilson
arxiv-2209-12269.description: Abstract We study the problem of deleting user data from machine learning models trained using empirical risk minimization. Our focus is on learning algorithms which return the empirical risk minimizer and approximate unlearning algorithms that comply with deletion requests that come streaming minibatches. Leveraging the infintesimal jacknife, we develop an online unlearning algorithm that is both computationally and memory efficient.

arxiv-2210-14773.description: Abstract . In a recent work, Duong, Ghoul and Zaag determined the gradient profile for blowup solutions of standard semilinear heat equation with power nonlinearities in the (supposed to be) generic case. Their method refines the constructive techniques introduced by Bricmont and Kupiainen and further developed by Merle and Zaag.

arxiv-2211-11128.creator: Constantin Kogler
arxiv-2211-11128.description: Abstract . We reduce the local limit theorem for a non-compact semisimple Lie group acting on its symmetric space to establishing that a natural operator associated to the measure is quasicompact. Under strong Diophantine assumptions on the underlying measure, we deduce the necessary spectral results for the operator in question.

arxiv-2310-19634.title: Iris: Dynamic Privacy Preserving Search in Authenticated Chord Peer-to-Peer Networks
arxiv-2310-19634.creator: Angeliki Aktypi, Kasper Rasmussen
arxiv-2310-19634.description: Abstract In structured peer-to-peer networks, like Chord, users find data by asking a number of intermediate nodes in the network. Each node provides the identity of the closet known node to the address of the data, until eventually the node responsible for the data is reached.

arxiv-2405-05043.title: Photon Squeezing in Photonic Time Crystals
arxiv-2405-05043.creator: Jaime Echave-Sustaeta, Francisco J. García-Vidal, P.A. Huidobro
arxiv-2405-05043.description: Abstract Time-varying media offer a platform to realize novel and exotic wave effects, including photonic time crystals characterized by momentum band gaps with exponential wave amplification. Here we focus on the quantum electrodynamical properties of time-varying media, in particular vacuum amplification and squeezing.

arxiv-2410-06992.title: SWE-Bench+: Enhanced Coding Benchmark for LLMs
arxiv-2410-06992.creator: Reem Aleithan, Haoran Xue, Mohammad Mahdi Mohajer, Elijah Nnorom, Gias Uddin, Song Wang
arxiv-2410-06992.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) in Software Engineering (SE) can offer assistance for coding. To facilitate a rigorous evaluation of LLMs in practical coding contexts, Carlos et al. introduced the SWE-bench dataset, which comprises 2,294 real-world GitHub issues and their corresponding pull requests, collected from 12 widely used Python repositories.

arxiv-2412-18175.title: Soliton Shielding of the focusing modified KdV equation
arxiv-2412-18175.creator: Ruihong Ma, Engui Fan ∗,
arxiv-2412-18175.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Ruihong Ma, Engui Fan ∗,. We consider soliton gas solutions of the modified Korteweg-de Vries (mKdV) equation, where the point spectrum of the condensate is located within a bounded domain in the upper half-plane. We first demonstrate that when the domain is a quadrature and the soliton density is an analytic function, the corresponding deterministic soliton gas coincides with a finite number of solitons, which we call this effect soliton shielding.

pmc-11367796.description: The major drawback to the implementation of genomic selection in a breeding program lies in long-term decrease in additive genetic variance, which is a trade-off for rapid genetic improvement in short term. Balancing increase in genetic gain with retention of additive genetic variance necessitates careful optimization of this trade-off.

pmc-11418005.title: Association of Aggression with Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms and Overactive Bladder in Men: Observations from a Large Population-representative Study
pmc-11418005.creator: Mikolaj Przydacz, Pawel Rajwa, Sabrina De Cillis, Cyrille Guillot-Tantay, Francois Herve, Antonio Tienza, Manuela Tutolo, Mehmet Gokhan Culha, Paolo Geretto, Nicholas Raison, Glenn T Werneburg, Marcin Miszczyk, Juan Gomez Rivas, Veronique Phe, Piotr Chlosta, Nadir Osman, European Association of Urol
pmc-11418005.description: Take Home MessageAggression was significantly associated with lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) and overactive bladder (OAB) according to our results. The link between aggression and LUTS/OAB was independent of age, comorbidities, and lifestyle habits. These results suggest that there is a need to screen for aggression among individuals who present with LUTS or OAB.

pmc-11573247.title: COVID-19 employment shocks and safety net expansion: Health effects on displaced workers☆
pmc-11573247.creator: Daniel Schneider, Kristen Harknett, Annette Gailliot
pmc-11573247.description: COVID-19 precipitated sharp job losses, concentrated in the service sector. Prior research suggests that such shocks would negatively affect health and wellbeing. However, the nature of the pandemic crisis was distinct in ways that may have mitigated any such negative effects, and historic expansions in unemployment insurance (UI) may have buffered workers from negative health consequences.

pmc-11631356.title: Prediction of 90 day readmission in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction by interpretable machine learning
pmc-11631356.creator: Baojia Zheng, Tao Liang, Jianping Mei, Xiuru Shi, Xiaohui Liu, Sikai Li, Yuting Wan, Yifeng Zheng, Xiaoyue Yang, Yanxia Huang
pmc-11631356.description: AimsCertain critical risk factors of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) patients were significantly different from those of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) patients, resulting in the limitations of existing predictive models in real‐world situations. This study aimed to develop a machine learning model for predicting 90 day readmission for HFpEF patients.

pmc-11651017.title: Successful endovascular therapy with “Direct tip injection in occlusive lesions (DIOL)” fashion for persistent sciatic artery aneurysmal occlusion: A case report
pmc-11651017.creator: Masanaga Tsujimoto, Takuya Haraguchi, Yoshifumi Kashima, Katsuhiko Sato, Tsutomu Fujita
pmc-11651017.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Persistent sciatic artery (PSA) is a rare congenital anomaly that may involve aneurysmal formations. During endovascular treatment for PSA aneurysm (PSAA) occlusion, guidewire crossing can be challenging due to complex anatomy. We report successful endovascular intervention for PSAA occlusion using the “direct tip injection in occlusive lesions (DIOL)” fashion, in which hydraulic pressure with contrast facilitates guidewire crossing by visualizing the vessel course and expanding the microchannel and vessel lumen.

pmc-12604632.creator: Mengfan Ding, R. Paul Ross, Eugene Dempsey, Bowen Li, Catherine Stanton
pmc-12604632.description: The infant gut microbiome undergoes a crucial transformation when solid foods enter the diet during weaning. This introduction normally happens at about six months post-birth and leads to major shifts in the gut microbiome. Many of the changes that occur during this period are known to persist into adulthood.

pmc-13493587.creator: Chao Liu, Chongxing Ji
pmc-13493587.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ClC-3 chloride channels play essential roles in cervical cancer progression by regulating lysosomal acidification, cell volume homeostasis, and chemoresistance. However, no highly selective small-molecule modulators of ClC-3 have been reported to date. Motivated by the urgent clinical need to reverse ClC-3-mediated chemoresistance and the challenge of processing massive chemical libraries under limited computational hardware resources, we propose a novel AI-driven Drug Discovery (AIDD) pipeline.
